              <li><span class="ds-anat-at is-small" style="--s:16px" data-icon="fist" aria-hidden="true"></span><span>16</span></li>
            </ul>
          </div>
          <p class="ds-note ds-anat-cap">The fist on its 24-unit grid, eight times up. The dashed square is the live area, two units in from the edge.</p>
        </div>

        <dl class="ds-laws">
          <div class="ds-law">
            <dt>One family</dt>
            <dd>Lucide, under the ISC licence, from <code>assets/icons/lucide</code>. The machine glyphs, the app icons and the showcase chrome all come from it, so nothing looks borrowed from another set.</dd>
          </div>
          <div class="ds-law">
            <dt>One stroke</dt>
            <dd>1.75 on the 24 grid, the size the app ships at. Marks at 16 px and below may go up to 2, so a small icon never thins out beside its label.</dd>
          </div>
          <div class="ds-law">
            <dt>Padded on the glass</dt>
            <dd>Each glyph sits in a 40-unit box around Lucide's 24, so the drawing spans about half its badge and the line stays near 3 to 4 glass pixels, bold enough for the queue. <span data-ds-glyphline></span></dd>
          </div>
          <div class="ds-law">
            <dt>Ink, not colour</dt>
            <dd>Icons draw in <code>currentColor</code>. Red reaches one only through its holder: the current tab, the strike, the red button.</dd>
          </div>
        </dl>
      </div>

              <button class="ds-pick" type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-run="karim" data-claimed="false">Crown unclaimed</button>
            </div>
            <button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-ds-replay="stats">Play the eight seconds again</button>
          </div>
          <div class="ds-secblocks" data-ds-secblocks="machine/stats"></div>
          <button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-go-mode="machine" data-go-mscreen="stats">Open Your run</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-yrcut">
        <h3 class="ds-h3">What left the glass</h3>
        <dl class="ds-cutlist">
          <div><dt>Energy, force, speed, acceleration</dt><dd>One pad reading in four units nobody here uses. They rise and fall with the score and add nothing to it.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Global, country and city ranks</dt><dd>Out of reach tonight, so they read as failure. They move to the app as long goals.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>The four rank grid</dt><dd>Four numbers of one kind make the eye compare them, and none changes what the player does next. Height and the crown say it.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>The replay still</dt><dd>The Result just played it. The impact frame moves to the crown takeover and the phone.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Percentages and comparisons</dt><dd>Numerals outside the one numbered block, and "as hard as a car crash" is not true. Words say it only when it is.</dd></div>
        </dl>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-parts">
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Where it came from</p>
          <p class="ds-p">An AI panel of four expert lenses, sensor science, arcade design, social play and information design, argued what a punch machine should show, and a synthesis settled where they disagreed. Its answer is in <code>docs/strategy/what-to-show-for-a-punch.md</code>.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Built as it says</p>
          <p class="ds-p">Four sections in its order and its five ideas for each. The gap is rounded up and never shown when it is more than fifteen per cent of the score. A person beats a line, and the machine sets its own mark when nobody is in reach.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Changed after it</p>
          <p class="ds-p">The old screen and its twenty designs were deleted and it was renamed Your run. The Big score dropped its ranks too. The build added what the paper left open: the bands fitted between the shared header and strip, the live score picks the nearest run, each hit is a still from the player's own shoot, and an eight second story plays the sections in its reading order.</p>
        </article>
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ============ the strike in numbers (the phone's Your hit, Stats; mpages/hit.js; docs/strategy/strike-in-numbers.md) ============ -->
    <section class="ds-sec" id="ds-strike" aria-labelledby="dsh-strike">
      <div class="ds-sec-head">
        <h2 class="ds-h2" id="dsh-strike" tabindex="-1">The strike in numbers</h2>
        <p class="ds-sec-lede">The glass shows one number. The fuller reading lives on the phone's Your hit, and its first version got it wrong: one pad reading in four units nobody in a Dubai mall uses, two of them impossible. Research into punch machines, punch trackers and the sports science of a punch replaced them with five numbers a player can picture and repeat, each rounded to what the pad can honestly claim and tagged with where it came from.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-strikebox">
        <figure class="ds-strikeview">
          <div class="m-app ds-app ds-strikeapp" inert>
            <div class="m-bg" aria-hidden="true"><div class="ms-lights"><i class="l1"></i><i class="l2"></i><i class="l3"></i><i class="l4"></i><i class="l5"></i><i class="l6"></i></div><span class="m-sheen"></span></div>
            <div class="ds-app-in yh ds-strikein" data-ds-strike></div>
          </div>
          <figcaption class="ds-note" data-ds-strikecap>A copy of the section on the phone's Your hit, as it is drawn now.</figcaption>
        </figure>
        <div class="ds-liveside">
          <div class="ds-secblocks" data-ds-secblocks="phone/hit" data-ds-only="stats"></div>
          <button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="hit">Open Your hit</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3 class="ds-h3 ds-sub ds-nums-h">Five numbers, each with its source</h3>
      <p class="ds-note ds-sub-note">The value beside each is read from the hit on the phone right now. Measured is a solid dot, your history a ring, this machine a bar and the camera a broken ring, so an estimate never looks like a reading.</p>
      <ol class="ds-nums m-app ds-tokens">
        <li class="ds-num">
          <div class="ds-num-h"><p class="ds-num-t">Peak force</p><span class="yx-tag" data-tag="measured">Measured</span></div>
          <p class="ds-num-v" data-ds-num="kg">about 315 kg, 15 past the bell</p>
          <p class="ds-num-p">In kilograms, the unit the UAE uses and the one Japanese punch machines taught players to boast in. Rounded to 5 and always worded about, because a good pad reads within about a tenth. The sensor reads on past the bell, so two bell ringers still differ.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="ds-num">
          <div class="ds-num-h"><p class="ds-num-t">On your last hit</p><span class="yx-tag" data-tag="history">Your history</span></div>
          <p class="ds-num-v" data-ds-num="change">+30 kg on your last</p>
          <p class="ds-num-p">The first question every tracker answers. A change under a twentieth of the hit reads About the same, so an ordinary wobble never reads as a decline.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="ds-num">
          <div class="ds-num-h"><p class="ds-num-t">Your best</p><span class="yx-tag" data-tag="history">Your history</span></div>
          <p class="ds-num-v" data-ds-num="best">This one, a new best</p>
          <p class="ds-num-p">The one comparison that is always fair, and a reason to scan: without the app, no best is kept.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="ds-num">
          <div class="ds-num-h"><p class="ds-num-t">Most hits here today</p><span class="yx-tag" data-tag="machine">This machine</span></div>
          <p class="ds-num-v" data-ds-num="band">100 to 175 kg, well above</p>
          <p class="ds-num-p">The middle half of today's hits on this pad, never an Olympian or a car crash, and one kind word for where yours sits: well above, in the middle or on the way up. It never says below.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="ds-num">
          <div class="ds-num-h"><p class="ds-num-t">Hand speed</p><span class="yx-tag" data-tag="camera">Camera estimate</span></div>
          <p class="ds-num-v is-est" data-ds-num="kmh">about 31 km/h</p>
          <p class="ds-num-p">Shown only when the camera runs at 120 frames a second or more and sees the arm from an angle, set thinner than what the pad measures, and never in mph. Speed barely separates beginners from boxers, so it is where a smaller friend can win.</p>
        </li>
        <li class="ds-num ds-num-reads">
          <div class="ds-num-h"><p class="ds-num-t">Seen on camera</p><span class="yx-tag" data-tag="read">Camera read</span></div>
          <p class="ds-num-v is-est" data-ds-num="reads">Right hand, stepped in</p>
          <p class="ds-num-p">Words, not figures: which hand, and whether the front foot stepped in. They explain the number beside them.</p>
        </li>
      </ol>

      <div class="ds-yrcut">
        <h3 class="ds-h3">What left the phone</h3>
        <dl class="ds-cutlist">
          <div><dt>Energy, 1.9 kJ</dt><dd>About fifteen times what an Olympic straight punch carries, the score worked backwards, in a unit nobody can feel.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Speed, 24.8 mph</dt><dd>The wrong unit for the UAE, and 11.1 m/s, faster than the Olympic boxers' average. A pad cannot see the fist at all.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Force, 3.1 kN</dt><dd>A fair reading in a unit nobody pictures. It stayed, as about 315 kg.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Acceleration</dt><dd>It describes the pad, not the fist, and rises and falls with the score.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>The radar</dt><dd>Four axes drawn from one reading make the same diamond for every hit, only larger or smaller.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Bars against the record</dt><dd>They put a bell hit at 83 to 89 per cent while its own chip said first at this machine.</dd></div>
        </dl>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-parts">
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Where it came from</p>
          <p class="ds-p">A research pass read the manuals of arcade boxers and Japanese kg machines, the punch trackers from Hykso to PowerKube, venue apps like Toptracer and Strava, and seven studies of how hard and fast people punch. Its answer is in <code>docs/strategy/strike-in-numbers.md</code>.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Rounded to the pad</p>
          <p class="ds-p">Kilograms to 5 and km/h to 1, in one place, <code>strikeOf</code> in <code>mobile.js</code>. One hit to the next varies by 5 to 10 per cent even for elite boxers, so nothing claims more than that.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Every state drawn</p>
          <p class="ds-p">Each design handles a hit past the bell, no speed reading, a first hit tonight, a player who has not scanned and a band not yet settled, which then reads this week.</p>
        </article>
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ============ flow states: Connected and Payment failed (parts/mpage-connected.html, mpage-failed.html) ============ -->
    <section class="ds-sec" id="ds-states" aria-labelledby="dsh-states">
      <div class="ds-sec-head">
        <h2 class="ds-h2" id="dsh-states" tabindex="-1">Flow states</h2>
        <p class="ds-sec-lede">Two phone pages the flow passes through rather than visits. Connected lands once the phone is linked to a machine, and Payment failed lands when a payment does not go through. Neither has a tab bar. Each says first what happened to the player's credit or money, then offers one way on and one way back.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-states">
        <article class="ds-panel ds-state">
          <p class="ds-k ds-dflt-k"><span data-lucide="link" aria-hidden="true"></span>Play</p>
          <h3 class="ds-dflt-t">Connected</h3>
          <ol class="ds-path" aria-label="Where Connected sits in the play flow">
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="scan">Scan</button></li>
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="connect">Connect</button></li>
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="connected" aria-current="step">Connected</button></li>
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="punch">Punch</button></li>
          </ol>
          <ul class="ds-state-rules">
            <li>The link, the chosen logo and the machine by name: Dubai Mall, by the Ice Rink, Machine 07, with the credit held for this turn.</li>
            <li>It goes on to Punch by itself after two and a half seconds, or at once on a tap, and a fill in Next step shows the wait.</li>
            <li>Cancel frees the machine and gives the credit back. Opened from the page bar it holds still, as a practice go that takes nothing.</li>
          </ul>
          <div class="ds-secblocks" data-ds-secblocks="phone/connected"></div>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-panel ds-state">
          <p class="ds-k ds-dflt-k"><span data-lucide="credit-card" aria-hidden="true"></span>Pay</p>
          <h3 class="ds-dflt-t">Payment failed</h3>
          <ol class="ds-path" aria-label="Where Payment failed sits in the pay flow">
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="topup">Buy credits</button></li>
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="checkout">Checkout</button></li>
            <li><button class="ds-path-s" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="failed" aria-current="step">Payment failed</button></li>
            <li><button class="ds-path-s ds-path-back" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="checkout">Try again</button></li>
          </ol>
          <ul class="ds-state-rules">
            <li>It opens on what did not happen: nothing was charged and no credit is held.</li>
            <li>The reason in plain words, this time's first: declined by the bank, cancelled before it finished, worded for Face ID, the fingerprint, PayPal or the card, or the connection dropped.</li>
            <li>Try again keeps the same pack and the same way to pay. Each way that did not fail is one tap into Checkout, and Back to the packs is always there.</li>
          </ul>
          <div class="ds-secblocks" data-ds-secblocks="phone/failed"></div>
        </article>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-parts">
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">The logo on the way in</p>
          <p class="ds-p">Connect, Connected, Punch and the Punch now button on Paid carry the chosen mark, the one the glass wears, so the phone and the machine read as one product at the moment they meet.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">One red move</p>
          <p class="ds-p">I'm at the pad on Connected, and Try again with its price on Payment failed. Everything else on either page is glass.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Punch on the machine</p>
          <p class="ds-p">After Connected, Punch keeps one title from the wait to the reading. Only the line under it changes, and its Machine section says Connected until the hit comes back.</p>
        </article>
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ============ the reel (parts/mpage-reel.html; mpages/reel.*, saved.js) ============ -->
    <section class="ds-sec" id="ds-reel" aria-labelledby="dsh-reel">
      <div class="ds-sec-head">
        <h2 class="ds-h2" id="dsh-reel" tabindex="-1">The reel</h2>
        <p class="ds-sec-lede">The reel plays everyone's hits without end, one at a time full screen or four to a screen in a grid. Any hit can be marked to keep from the reel's tools, a feed post or the header of Your hit. The mark is the whole of it: there are no lists to manage and no page to file them in.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-reelbox">
        <figure class="ds-panel ds-rail">
          <div class="ds-rail-art m-app ds-app" aria-hidden="true">

              <span class="ds-rail-cell is-measured"><span class="ds-rail-i" data-icon="heart"></span><span class="ds-rail-n">2.4k</span></span>
              <span class="ds-rail-cell"><span class="ds-rail-i" data-lucide="message-circle"></span><span class="ds-rail-n">86</span></span>
              <span class="ds-rail-cell"><span class="ds-rail-i" data-lucide="bookmark"></span><span class="ds-rail-n">Save</span></span>
              <span class="ds-rail-cell"><span class="ds-rail-i" data-lucide="share-2"></span><span class="ds-rail-n">Share</span></span>

          <figcaption><b>The rail</b>The first of the Actions designs: one column, one icon size, every label centred under its icon. Its centre is the header's settings button's centre, and its last label ends on the foot of the words over the video. Split, the newest, breaks the same tools in two, the counts up the right edge and the three tools in a row at the foot.</figcaption>
        </figure>
        <div class="ds-reelside">
          <h3 class="ds-h3">Two views</h3>
          <dl class="ds-laws ds-views">
            <div class="ds-law"><dt><span data-lucide="rectangle-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></span>Full screen</dt><dd>One attempt at a time with its score, place and tools. Only the attempt in view plays, and the next one loads behind it. Its three sections are the ones Customise lists.</dd></div>
            <div class="ds-law"><dt><span data-lucide="grid-2x2" aria-hidden="true"></span>Grid</dt><dd>Two in a row and four to a screen, from the same endless list. A tap opens that attempt full screen, and the videos in view play muted. It has one composition and nothing to choose, so it carries no row.</dd></div>
          </dl>

            <button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-ds-reel="full">Open the reel</button>
            <button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-ds-reel="grid">Open the grid</button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3 class="ds-h3 ds-sub ds-save-h">Saving a hit</h3>
      <p class="ds-note ds-sub-note">Keeping a hit used to mean a page of named lists to file it in. Almost nobody sorts a reel, so the lists and the page went and the save became one mark on the attempt, the same mark wherever that attempt appears.</p>
      <ul class="ds-savesteps">
        <li><p class="ds-savestep-t"><span data-lucide="bookmark" aria-hidden="true"></span>Tap</p><p class="ds-note">Marks the attempt, the mark fills, and a toast says Saved for later. Nothing asks where it went.</p></li>
        <li><p class="ds-savestep-t"><span data-lucide="x" aria-hidden="true"></span>Tap again</p><p class="ds-note">Takes the mark off and says so. The button is the same control both ways, so there is nothing to undo.</p></li>
        <li><p class="ds-savestep-t"><span data-lucide="layers" aria-hidden="true"></span>One mark, everywhere</p><p class="ds-note">The reel's tools, a feed post and the header of Your hit all draw the same hit, so marking it in one place fills it in the others at once.</p></li>
        <li><p class="ds-savestep-t"><span data-lucide="history" aria-hidden="true"></span>It survives a reload</p><p class="ds-note">The marks keep to the phone in <code>punch-saved.v2</code>, and a blocked store only shortens their life to this visit.</p></li>
      </ul>
      <p class="ds-note ds-save-foot">Any button with <code>data-save-key</code> carries the mark with no script of its own: <code>mpages/saved.js</code> listens once for the whole app, writes the key and fires <code>saved</code>, which repaints every button drawn on that hit. <code>window.punchSaved</code> exposes has, save, remove and paint for a page that draws its own.</p>

      <div class="ds-secblocks ds-reelsecs" data-ds-secblocks="phone/reel"></div>
      <div class="ds-rowbtns"><button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-go-mode="mobile" data-go-page="reel">Open the reel</button></div>
    </section>

    <!-- ============ the showcase's own loader (#loader in index.html, styles.css loader block) ============ -->
    <section class="ds-sec" id="ds-loader" aria-labelledby="dsh-loader">
      <div class="ds-sec-head">
        <h2 class="ds-h2" id="dsh-loader" tabindex="-1">Loader</h2>
        <p class="ds-sec-lede">The first thing the showcase shows is the lockup, a thin bar and one line of type. Nothing else. It used to be the strength tester in miniature, with a puck that climbed and a count that lit a digit at a time, which made the wait look like the thing the player came for and stole the score's one entrance. It draws in the look already chosen, before any script arrives.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-panel ds-ldpanel">
        <div class="ds-ldstage" data-ds-ld aria-hidden="true"></div>
        <div class="ds-ldctl">
          <div class="ds-ctl">
            <label for="ds-ld-charge">Progress</label><output id="ds-ld-out" for="ds-ld-charge">Full</output>
            <input type="range" id="ds-ld-charge" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="100" data-ds-ldrange>
          </div>
          <button class="ds-look-btn" type="button" data-ds-ldplay>Play a load</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="ds-parts ds-parts-4">
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">One value</p>
          <p class="ds-p"><code>--lp</code> scales the bar and nothing else. A clock under the markup eases it toward the real progress app.js reports, so it never sits still and never runs ahead.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Nothing to decode</p>
          <p class="ds-p">A bar says how far along in a glance, which is all a wait has to say. The mark holds the brand and the line says what is happening, in the label face the rest of the showcase uses.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Quiet while it shows</p>
          <p class="ds-p">Focus stays put and a screen reader hears one polite line, then Ready. With reduced motion the bar is simply full and only its fade moves.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">It cannot outstay</p>
          <p class="ds-p">The bar is 320 px at most and never wider than the phone it is on. A CSS failsafe fades the whole screen at nine seconds, so a script that never arrives cannot hold the page.</p>
        </article>
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ============ components ============ -->
    <section class="ds-sec" id="ds-components" aria-labelledby="dsh-components">
      <div class="ds-sec-head">
        <h2 class="ds-h2" id="dsh-components" tabindex="-1">Components</h2>
        <p class="ds-sec-lede">Drawn with the same classes the machine and the app use, not redrawn for this page. Machine parts sit in a scaled piece of the glass; app parts sit on the app's own ground.</p>
      </div>

      <h3 class="ds-h3 ds-sub">On the machine</h3>

    <!-- ============ the machine flow ============ -->
    <section class="ds-sec" id="ds-flow" aria-labelledby="dsh-flow">
      <div class="ds-sec-head">
        <h2 class="ds-h2" id="dsh-flow" tabindex="-1">Machine flow</h2>
        <p class="ds-sec-lede">Around the result, eight more screens run on the glass, from Home at rest to a new record. Each is one frame of sections, and every screen carries the same three shared parts in the same place: the background behind it, the header at the top and the sponsor strip at the foot. The four result screens share a fourth, Punch again. The showcase opens the glass at actual size, a glass pixel to a screen pixel whenever the window is wide enough.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="ds-flowbox">
        <figure class="ds-flowview">
          <div class="ds-flowglass"><iframe data-ds-flowframe title="The machine glass, showing the chosen flow screen" tabindex="-1" loading="lazy"></iframe></div>
          <figcaption class="ds-note" data-ds-flowcap>The glass loads when this section comes into view.</figcaption>
        </figure>
        <div class="ds-flowside">
          <h3 class="ds-h3">Screens</h3>
          <ul class="ds-flowlist" data-ds-flowlist></ul>
          <h3 class="ds-h3 ds-flowh">Background</h3>
          <p class="ds-note">Preview any of the eight on this glass only. The one the phone and the machine share is chosen under Background, above, or in Customise.</p>
          <div class="ds-picks" role="group" aria-label="Preview a backdrop" data-ds-backdrops></div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3 class="ds-h3 ds-sub ds-flowh">The shared parts</h3>
      <div class="ds-parts ds-parts-4 ds-parts-flow">
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Background</p>
          <p class="ds-p"><code>.ms-lights</code> with six lights, the first child of every screen and the same host the phone carries. Eight looks, all CSS, all still under reduced motion.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Header</p>
          <p class="ds-p"><code>.ms-head</code>, one choice of five for every screen: Lockup, Venue and clock, Slim bar, Crest and Stacked. It keeps one band at the top, so the brand never jumps between states.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Sponsor strip</p>
          <p class="ds-p">A 1080 by 140 strip at the foot of every screen, one creative of five for all of them: Lightning, Score deal, Claw rip, Flavours and Split. Monster Energy, in hard cuts on a short loop, with its call in green that stays put. Reduced motion holds the frame that carries the message.</p>
        </article>
        <article class="ds-part">
          <p class="ds-k">Punch again</p>
          <p class="ds-p"><code>parts/ms-again.html</code>, the close of every result screen: the Result, the Big score and New record. A 200 px band over the strip in five designs, Full button, Button pair, Countdown, Code handoff and Big pad, and it plays in last.</p>
        </article>
      </div>
    </section>

  <div class="help-point">
    <h3>Customise works per screen</h3>
    <p>Every screen is a stack of sections, and each section is drawn several ways. <b>Customise</b> opens on whatever screen is in front of you and pages through that screen's own designs. Under it, <b>Across the showcase</b> holds what both surfaces share: theme, background, logo, phone model, score format. Choices survive a reload.</p>
  </div>

    <!-- ========== Payment failed: the payment did not go through (mpages/failed.css, mpages/failed.js) ==========
         Reached from Checkout when a payment fails (the demo row there makes one fail: declined, cancelled or offline);
         pay.js keeps the pack and the way to pay, and window.punchPay says what happened and runs the buttons.
         The pay pages' frame (pay.css .pay-top, .pay-body, .pay-foot): the header keeps the unchanged balance in view,
         the body says what happened, why and what else to do, and the footer's Try again goes back to the same checkout.
         Built from sections (psec.js), five designs each, chosen in Customise under This screen:
           What happened  Cross, Slip, Wallet, Banner, Photo (every copy filled from [data-fail-f])
           Why            List, Tabs, Most likely, Plain, Questions (the reason this time first, the other two after it)
           What to do     Ways, Chips, Buttons, Wallet first, Pack kept (drawn by failed.js: the ways to pay that did not
                          fail, and Back to the packs) -->
